20.text: The name of the reindeer is generally taken from its color or from some

21.text: peculiar feature of its antlers. Examples of such names are The-quite-Black-

22.text: One, One-with-a-Cross-Branch-over-the-Forehead, etc. Some breeders give real

23.text: names to a few reindeer of their herds: e. g., Young-Lamut-Reindeer (Tor-

24.text: waˊwaq), — though this name was given to a Chukchee reindeer partly for

25.text: the purpose of increasing its agility through the force of the word. — Mush-

27.text: The term of a reindeer’s life is from twelve to fifteen years, though some

28.text: animals live considerably longer. According to age, they are classified as

32.text: Pêˊêčvak (both male and female), less than one year old.

33.text: Peˊnvel (male) and vañqaˊs˙-qor (female), from one to two years old.

34.text: Krɪmɪˊntɪ (male) and krɪˊm-qor (female), from two to three years old.

42.text: Čŭˊmñɪñ (“buck”), more than seven years old.

43.text: The reindeer begins to shed its hair in the spring, and finishes in the

44.text: middle of summer. Well-fed animals start shedding before lean ones, and

45.text: grown animals before younger ones. A herd in good condition will finish

46.text: two weeks earlier than a lean one. The new hair is short and sleek, but it

47.text: thickens rapidly; and in September the skins of fawns are suitable for making

48.text: winter garments. For this purpose skins of fawns are used almost exclusively.

49.text: The fawns are killed at two set periods in early fall, according to the kind

50.text: of fur desired. The late fall fawn-skins are used only for heavy overcoats;

51.text: and the skins of grown animals, for sleeping-room coverings, bedding, and the

52.text: like. For the Russian trade, spring fawn-skins of smaller size, called by the

53.text: traders “vyporotki” (выпоротки), are required. Of these, the black skins are
